analysis:
Examined both release-document excerpts, the complete base/head component router and patch, and file metadata, including the unchanged executable mode of scripts/ci-tested-tree.py. No independently supported security regression was identified in this scope. scripts/ci-component-paths.py:131–145 now path-selects PRs into master/main instead of forcing every component. Provider sources, libraries, fixtures and shared CI controls still select their mapped components; SHA validation, merge-base comparison and NUL-delimited rename-inclusive path handling remain intact. This reduces blanket test coverage but does not itself demonstrate bypass of a security control.

Docs/operations/provider-release.md:499–541 describe scheduled/manual dev publication, inherited secrets, source verification and changed concurrency; these are claims requiring comparison with the changed workflows, not proof of enforcement. Surrounding signing, exact-byte publication, qualification and rollback contracts were examined against A-005, A-011, A-017, T-013, T-054 and T-043. No supplied change directly alters inference encryption, tenant cache isolation (T-008/T-041), credential custody, authorization or billing.

Integration must reconcile path selection with the changed tested-tree reuse logic. The bounded scripts/ci-tested-tree.py patch describes new tree-only records for squash/exact-tree pushes, but its implementation is absent from primary units and the excerpt is truncated. Verify successful-run provenance, same-workflow/repository restrictions, actual tested-tree binding and component-mask coverage before allowing a master push to skip tests; inspect its workflow callers and record producers. Also verify scheduled dispatch admission and secret isolation against docs/provider-release.md:504–534. Missing source limits this pass; it is not evidence of a vulnerability or safety.
